title: HELIX: Verified compilation of cyber-physical control systems to LLVM IR
abstract: This paper presents the design of HELIX, an end-to-end verified code generation system with a focus on the intersection of high-performance and high-assurance numerical computing. The code generation can be fine-tuned to generate efficient code for a broad set of computer architectures while providing formal guarantees of the correctness of such generated code. Using a real-life example of a cyber-physical robot system, this paper demonstrates how, by using HELIX, one can start from a high-level mathematical formulation of the problem, apply a series of algebraic transformations that target intermediate languages, and generate an efficient imperative implementation. This is done while formally verifying semantic preservation from the original formulation down to LLVM IR. The method we used for high-performance code compilation is the algebraic transformation of vector and matrix computations into a dataflow optimised for parallel or vectorised processing on target hardware. The abstraction used to formalise and verify this technique is an operator language and accompanying semantics-preserving term rewriting. We use sparse vector abstraction to represent partial computations, enabling us to use algebraic reasoning to prove parallel decomposition properties. HELIX's verification infrastructure comprises multiple intermediate languages and verification approaches, all implemented in the Coq proof assistant. In particular, it uses verified term rewriting, translation validation, metaprogramming, verified compilation, layered monadic interpreters; it also supports application-specific uses of (verified) numerical analysis as we demonstrate via the running example.

title: UMI-Underwater: Learning Underwater Manipulation without Underwater Teleoperation
abstract: Underwater robotic grasping is difficult due to degraded, highly variable imagery and the expense of collecting diverse underwater demonstrations. We introduce a system that (i) autonomously collects successful underwater grasp demonstrations via a self-supervised data collection pipeline and (ii) transfers grasp knowledge from on-land human demonstrations through a depth-based affordance representation that bridges the on-land-to-underwater domain gap and is robust to lighting and color shift. An affordance model trained on on-land handheld demonstrations is deployed underwater zero-shot via geometric alignment, and an affordance-conditioned diffusion policy is then trained on underwater demonstrations to generate control actions. In pool experiments, our approach improves grasping performance and robustness to background shifts, and enables generalization to objects seen only in on-land data, outperforming RGB-only baselines. Code, videos, and additional results are available at https://umi-under-water.github.io.

title: OVI-MAP:Open-Vocabulary Instance-Semantic Mapping
abstract: Incremental open-vocabulary 3D instance-semantic mapping is essential for autonomous agents operating in complex everyday environments. However, it remains challenging due to the need for robust instance segmentation, real-time processing, and flexible open-set reasoning. Existing methods often rely on the closed-set assumption or dense per-pixel language fusion, which limits scalability and temporal consistency. We introduce OVI-MAP that decouples instance reconstruction from semantic inference. We propose to build a class-agnostic 3D instance map that is incrementally constructed from RGB-D input, while semantic features are extracted only from a small set of automatically selected views using vision-language models. This design enables stable instance tracking and zero-shot semantic labeling throughout online exploration. Our system operates in real time and outperforms state-of-the-art open-vocabulary mapping baselines on standard benchmarks.

evidence.title: OVI-MAP:Open-Vocabulary Instance-Semantic Mapping
evidence.abstract: Incremental open-vocabulary 3D instance-semantic mapping is essential for autonomous agents operating in complex everyday environments. However, it remains challenging due to the need for robust instance segmentation, real-time processing, and flexible open-set reasoning. Existing methods often rely on the closed-set assumption or dense per-pixel language fusion, which limits scalability and temporal consistency. We introduce OVI-MAP that decouples instance reconstruction from semantic inference. We propose to build a class-agnostic 3D instance map that is incrementally constructed from RGB-D input, while semantic features are extracted only from a small set of automatically selected views using vision-language models. This design enables stable instance tracking and zero-shot semantic labeling throughout online exploration. Our system operates in real time and outperforms state-of-the-art open-vocabulary mapping baselines on standard benchmarks.

title: GLASS: Geometry-aware Local Alignment and Structure Synchronization Network for 2D-3D Registration
abstract: Image-to-point cloud registration methods typically follow a coarse-to-fine pipeline, extracting patch-level correspondences and refining them into dense pixel-to-point matches. However, in scenes with repetitive patterns, images often lack sufficient 3D structural cues and alignment with point clouds, leading to incorrect matches. Moreover, prior methods usually overlook structural consistency, limiting the full exploitation of correspondences. To address these issues, we propose two novel modules: the Local Geometry Enhancement (LGE) module and the Graph Distribution Consistency (GDC) module. LGE enhances both image and point cloud features with normal vectors, injecting geometric structure into image features to reduce mismatches. GDC constructs a graph from matched points to update features and explicitly constrain similarity distributions. Extensive experiments and ablations on two benchmarks, RGB-D Scenes v2 and 7-Scenes, demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in image-to-point cloud registration.

title: PAD-Hand: Physics-Aware Diffusion for Hand Motion Recovery
abstract: Significant advancements made in reconstructing hands from images have delivered accurate single-frame estimates, yet they often lack physics consistency and provide no notion of how confidently the motion satisfies physics. In this paper, we propose a novel physics-aware conditional diffusion framework that refines noisy pose sequences into physically plausible hand motion while estimating the physics variance in motion estimates. Building on a MeshCNN-Transformer backbone, we formulate Euler-Lagrange dynamics for articulated hands. Unlike prior works that enforce zero residuals, we treat the resulting dynamic residuals as virtual observables to more effectively integrate physics. Through a last-layer Laplace approximation, our method produces per-joint, per-time variances that measure physics consistency and offers interpretable variance maps indicating where physical consistency weakens. Experiments on two well-known hand datasets show consistent gains over strong image-based initializations and competitive video-based methods. Qualitative results confirm that our variance estimations are aligned with the physical plausibility of the motion in image-based estimates.

title: TALKING TO MACHINES: A CORRELATIONAL STUDY OF EXTRAVERSION AND EMOTIONAL ATTACHMENT TO AI CHATBOTS
authors: SILLA JACOB 1 MANJULIKA KARMAKAR 2 JUHI SOLAMAN 3
abstract: Abstract: The increasing use of AI chatbots has changed the way people seek information and support. Users start to develop emotional bonds with these chatbots as they become more conversational. However, it is unclear whether certain aspects of personality influence the strength of these connections. This study aims to understand if there exists a correlation between extraversion and level of emotional attachment to AI chatbots. Data were collected from undergraduate students aged 18-25 who have interacted with AI. Participants completed a self-report questionnaire consisting of two sections: one assessing their extraversion and another measuring their emotional attachment to AI, both using a Likert-type scale. It was hypothesized that a relationship between extraversion and level of attachment to AI chatbots does exist, with individuals lower in extraversion expected to report stronger attachment. The collected data will be analyzed using correlational statistical methods to determine whether the hypothesis is supported. AI chatbots are increasingly used for assistance and everyday problem-solving, which may affect the ways individuals emotionally respond to these systems. Understanding the psychological aspects that affect user engagement becomes even more important as interactions with AI increase. Examining the relationship between personality traits and emotional attachment to AI may contribute to the growing field of human–AI interaction research. The results of this study may shed light on how various personality traits affect how people relate to and engage with AI-based communication tools. Keywords: Generative Artificial Intelligence, AI Dependency, Academic Performance, Technostress, Cognitive Engagement, Higher Education.

title: Data and Scripts for the paper "Signification Index"
abstract: We study whether different projection types within transformer neural networks develop systematically different levels of structural order during training. Using the Signification Index (S), a bounded metric in [0, 1] derived from the spectral entropy of weight matrix singular value decompositions, we analyze checkpoints from four language models spanning three architecture families, three training datasets, and two orders of magnitude in parameter count (160M to 70B parameters). We report two observational findings. First, at mature training stages (defined as tokens-per-parameter T/P ≥ 25), the MLP expansion projection consistently achieves a higher S than the contraction projection in all four models, regardless of whether this ordering holds from the start of training or emerges after a transient reversal. Second, in the two models with standard split attention projections (Amber-7B and OLMo-1B), the query projection achieves the highest S among query, key, and value projections at mature training stages. We discuss a plausible functional interpretation, i.e., projections serving more generative or query-generating roles may develop richer spectral geometry, while being explicit that the present study is observational, the sample of four models is small, and causal claims are not warranted. All data and analysis scripts are made available to support reproducibility.

title: Photovoltaic (PV) Generation Dataset with Orientation Diversity
abstract: This dataset contains hourly photovoltaic (PV) generation data and associated input variables collected from an experimental rooftop PV system. The dataset includes temporal, meteorological, and orientation-related features used for short-term PV power forecasting. Measurements were recorded at an hourly resolution over approximately one year (7080 hours). The dataset consists of the following variables: - Day: Day of the year - Cosine of Day: Cyclical representation of the day of the year - Hour: Hour of the day - Cosine of Hour: Cyclical representation of the hour of the day - Air Temperature (°C) - Dew Point (°C) - Wind Speed (m/s) - Air Pressure (hPa) - Weather Condition: Categorical weather description - Solar Radiation (W/m²) For each PV panel (PV-1 to PV-5), the following variables are provided: - Cosine value of the solar incidence angle - Measured PV power output (W or Wh) Additionally: - Total PV Power: Aggregated power output of all panels The PV system consists of multiple panels with different tilt and azimuth configurations, enabling the analysis of orientation-aware PV forecasting under identical environmental conditions. This repository includes raw and processed data along with variable descriptions to support reproducible research in photovoltaic forecasting and energy systems. ## CitationIf you use this dataset in academic work, please cite: "Short-term forecasting of rooftop photovoltaic energy generation using machine learning techniques", PeerJ Computer Science. ## LicenseThis dataset is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license.

title: HYBRID CONTROL SYSTEM FOR SPRAY DRYING OF EXTRACT WITH NEURO-FUZZY CORRECTION OF SETPOINTS
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid control system for spray drying of extract, aimed at improving the accuracy of moisture stabilization of the dried product in the presence of crosscouplings between control loops and external disturbances caused by variations in raw material properties and air environment parameters. The basic control structure preserves the con-ventional industrial implementation of local PID control loops, while the coordination of in-teracting loops is performed at a supervisory level in the form of an ANFIS-based setpoint corrector. The corrector generates incremental adjustments to the setpoints of the inlet drying-agent temperature and its flow rate based on the current values of outlet gas temperature, product moisture content, and absolute humidity of the inlet air. This architecture enables par-tial compensation of mutual interactions between process channels without altering the struc-ture of local PID control or requiring modifications to the hardware configuration of the sys-tem.The mathematical model of the process was developed in the MATLAB/Simulink en-vironment by identifying individual channels using static characteristics and dynamic re-sponses within a selected operating range, followed by approximation with transfer functions including dead time. Model adequacy was confirmed by comparing simulated output varia-bles with published experimental data from open sources and by iterative refinement of trans-fer-function parameters until a mean relative error of 3% was achieved. Since experimental data from an actual industrial installation were unavailable for training the neuro-fuzzy model, ANFIS training was performed using training datasets generated in the simulation environ-ment based on the developed mathematical model, static dependencies, and a series of simula-tion runs.The effectiveness of the proposed approach was evaluated through comparative simu-lation of a conventional PID-based control system and a hybrid system with ANFIS-based setpoint correction. Performance indicators included overshoot, settling time, and the integral squared error (ISE) criterion under a baseline operating scenario. It was established that the application of the ANFIS corrector reduces the settling time by 33 % (from 180 to 120 s), de-creases overshoot by a factor of 2.4 (from 12 % to 5 %), and lowers the ISE value by 48 % (from 1.00 to 0.52) compared with the PID-only control system. Further research should focus on experimental validation of the proposed algorithm on real equipment, additional training of the ANFIS model using experimental data, and assessment of the supervisory control layer performance in the presence of measurement noise and actuator constraints.

title: Using recurrence microstates to improve learning of multi-layer perceptrons
abstract: Abstract Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), particularly the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), have become popular for modeling complex functions and solving nonlinear problems. Despite their success, the difficulty in interpreting their internal processes hinders the understanding of many physicists of how hyperparameters, input data, and training techniques influence convergence and overall model performance. In this study, we propose the use of recurrence analysis as an additional tool to examine the dynamic behavior of MLP networks during the learning process. Here, the learning process refers to the supervised classification of different dynamical regimes, where each class corresponds to a distinct parameter value of the underlying system. We apply the methodology to several well-known dynamical systems: the generalized Bernoulli shift, logistic map, the Lorenz attractor, and long memory processes known as colored noise. The results indicate that the microstates quantification changes the way the network interprets the data, varying the weight of the connection between layers and forming patterns on connection weight matrices, especially for larger microstate sizes. Furthermore, we observe that the use of recurrence microstates enables the identification of overfitting, providing a more physically interpretable understanding of the network’s internal dynamics. In summary, recurrence analysis can be used as a complementary approach for interpreting and enhancing the performance of neural networks, especially in tasks involving complex data and dynamical systems.

title: A Comparative Study of PPO and SAC for End-to-End Visual Peg-in-Hole Insertion
abstract: Peg-in-hole insertion is a representative precision assembly task because it requires accurate alignment and stable contact handling in a small tolerance range. Conventional solutions usually depend on geometric modeling, calibration, and explicit pose estimation, which may reduce flexibility when the target condition changes. This paper presents an end-toend visual reinforcement learning framework for peg-in-hole insertion of a UR5 manipulator in simulation and focuses on a direct comparison between Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC). A PyBullet platform with an eye-in-hand camera is constructed, where the policy takes only grayscale images as observation and outputs continuous Cartesian displacement actions. Under a unified task definition, reward design, and evaluation protocol, the two methods are compared in terms of training process, nominal performance, and perturbed-condition evaluation. The results show that PPO has slightly higher per-step training throughput, whereas SAC reaches useful insertion behavior in fewer training steps, achieves a higher final reward and success rate, and exhibits stronger robustness under perturbations. These results indicate that, for the studied end-to-end visual insertion task, SAC provides better overall training efficiency and policy quality than PPO.

title: Security Analysis of the BB84 Quantum Key Distribution Protocol Using Qiskit
abstract: The rapid progress of quantum computing demands secure communication protocols which are beyond classical cryptographic techniques. This necessity of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is met by providing security relying on the fundamental laws of quantum mechanics. In the work presented, the BB84 protocol is implemented using Qiskit platform provided by IBM. The performance is analyzed for both the ideal channel conditions and an intercept–resend eavesdropping scenario studying its security behavior and performance. 100% key agreement is observed with a QBER of 0% for the BB84 protocol executed under the ideal condition. When an eavesdropper is introduced, the QBER increases significantly, ranging from 16% to 38%, exceeding the acceptable security threshold of 11% and resulting in complete rejection of the generated key. Performance analysis carried out for key sizes between 100 and 1000 qubits shows that the execution time follows O(n) trend growing linearly. This simulation validates the correct operation of the BB84 protocol and demonstrates a detailed performance and security analysis of a QKD system using IBM Qiskit.

title: An authenticated field-free multi-keyword data search scheme for the Internet of Health Things
abstract: Abstract In the Internet of Health Things (IoHT), patients upload encrypted health data to the cloud, enabling doctors to access records remotely, and make timely diagnoses beyond geographical limits. A potential challenge is the efficient retrieval of specific medical data by doctors from large-scale encrypted datasets. Identity-based encryption with keyword search offers a feasible solution and addresses certificate management problem. Multi-keyword search is essential in IoHT as it improves retrieval efficiency. This paper proposes an SM9-based authenticated field-free multi-keyword searchable encryption scheme. The proposed scheme overcomes the limitation of existing SM9-based searchable encryption schemes that only support single-keyword search and provides resistance against keyword guessing attack, enhancing both functionality and security. We use the polynomial technique to achieve multi-keyword search while eliminating keyword field restrictions, resulting in high flexibility. Our scheme is proven to satisfy secure index indistinguishability and search token indistinguishability. Theoretical analysis and experimental results demonstrate its effectiveness. In multi-keyword search scenarios, compared with existing SM9-based schemes that require repeated executions of the index generation algorithm, our scheme reduces computational overhead by at least $\sim $92% with a single execution and further decreases index storage cost by at least 45%. Moreover, it improves search efficiency by at least 73%, making it more suitable for the IoHT.

title: Agentic AI
abstract: At a technical level, artificial intelligence (AI) agents may seem complex, but the concept is surprisingly simple. Think of every agent as having three main parts: a goal, a brain, a toolbox, and memory. For a solo freelancer, AI agents are more than just a time-saver. They are a way to scale the abilities and transform one-person gig into a mini digital enterprise. Growth and business development includes automate high-level research, build passive income systems, and upskill while work. Client communication is one of the biggest time drains for freelancers. AI agents represent the ultimate evolution of the AI sidekick. The most user-friendly platform for a non-technical person to use to build an agent-like assistant is GPTs, a feature available in ChatGPT Plus. Alternative Platforms for Building Agents: Notion AI, Make.com, Zapier AI, and Relevance AI or CrewAI.

title: How Open Must Language Models be to Enable Reliable Scientific Inference?
abstract: How does the extent to which a model is open or closed impact the scientific inferences that can be drawn from research that involves it? In this paper, we analyze how restrictions on information about model construction and deployment threaten reliable inference. We argue that current closed models are generally ill-suited for scientific purposes, with some notable exceptions, and discuss ways in which the issues they present to reliable inference can be resolved or mitigated. We recommend that when models are used in research, potential threats to inference should be systematically identified along with the steps taken to mitigate them, and that specific justifications for model selection should be provided.

title: Advanced Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Short-Term Solar Radiation Forecasting Using Temporal and Meteorological Features
abstract: Short-term forecasting of solar radiation is essential for the efficient operation of solar energy systems. This study presents a neural network-based approach for short-term solar radiation forecasting using a hybrid framework that integrates temporal characteristics with weather-based features. The proposed model combines a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) to capture short-term temporal dynamics, a Transformer Encoder, and a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) to integrate these representations for final prediction. Key meteorological variables, including temperature, humidity, and wind speed, are incorporated along with engineered time-related features such as lagged values, rolling statistics, and cyclical time-of-day encodings. The results demonstrate that the hybrid model effectively integrates sequential learning and feature interaction, leading to improved forecasting accuracy. The proposed approach achieves a test Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.056, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.086, and coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.92, outperforming benchmark models such as AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), GRU, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). The model maintains stable performance across cross-validation folds, multiple forecasting horizons, and varying weather conditions. These findings indicate that the proposed framework provides a reliable and practical solution for accurate short-term solar radiation forecasting, supporting real-time solar energy management and renewable energy system optimization.

title: Intelligent Emergency Training System: A Study on Human-Computer Interaction Design Based on a Multimodal AI Agent
abstract: Critical emergency care relies on efficient multi-team collaboration and precise situational awareness, and its teaching methodologies are undergoing systematic transformation driven by the deep integration of digital technologies. Traditional blended (virtual-actual) teaching systems often function as isolated skill training tools, lacking effective support for constructing shared mental models and distributed cognition within teams. This study employs dynamic difficulty adaptation based on deep reinforcement learning as its core engine, utilizing a multimodal AI agent interaction interface, real-time collaborative network analysis, and counterfactual explanation feedback to construct an immersive human-computer collaboration relationship, thereby enhancing team decision-making transparency and debriefing efficiency. A quantitative study was conducted with 25 undergraduate nursing students to investigate the impact of the system's interaction design on individual and team emergency performance. The findings indicate that AI-driven dynamic difficulty adaptation significantly enhanced learners' flow experience, and the multimodal AI agent effectively reduced cognitive load during operations. However, its gaze guidance presented a risk of "cognitive tunneling" under high-pressure scenarios. While the team cognition enhancement interface improved debriefing efficiency, the issue of information overload requires further optimization.

title: The Construction of an AI-based chatbot to Provide Formative Feedback on Argumentative Writing
abstract: The study explores students’ perceptions of the efficacy of an AI-based chatbot "IELTS Writing Tutor" in providing formative feedback on argumentative essays to first-year engineering students at a China-UK collaborative undergraduate program. Built on the Smartutor platform, the chatbot delivers structured feedback aligned with IELTS Writing Task 2 criteria, model answers, and reflection prompts. 29 students engaged in the research and received feedback on the three writing responses they wrote. This study employed a mixed-methods approach. Quantitative data were collected via a 5-point Likert scale questionnaire measuring perceived usefulness and ease of use of the chatbot, followed by SPSS-based descriptive analysis. Qualitative data included open-ended feedback from students, which was analyzed using thematic analysis. The study found participants rated the chatbot highly on both usefulness and ease of use, with all mean scores exceeding 4.2. While its core strengths are recognized in promptly identifying errors and delivering learning-focused feedback, the findings indicate that future development must focus on two key areas: advancing personalized learning experience and diversifying modes of interaction.

title: Design and Implementation of a Lattice-Based Post-Quantum Secure Bootloader for RISC-V with QEMU-Based Validation
abstract: The rapid proliferation of RISC-V architectures in embedded, IoT, and safety-critical systems necessitates quantum-resistant secure boot mechanisms to counter harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks targeting classical RSA/ECDSA firmware signatures. This paper presents PQBoot-C, a complete 52 kB production-ready C implementation of a lattice-based post-quantum secure bootloader for RISC-V 64-bit processors featuring NIST-standardized Dilithium2 (ML-DSA) signature verification. PQBoot-C establishes a quantum-resilient hardware root-of-trust through a multi-stage PQChain verification protocol: SHA3-256 measured boot computes kernel integrity, Dilithium2 authenticates firmware against an embedded public key, and Physical Memory Protection (PMP) enforces hardware-isolated execution. Comprehensive QEMU RV64GCV emulation enables reproducible cycle-accurate profiling, demonstrating a bounded total secure boot cost of 1.43 million clock cycles, corresponding to 14.3 ms on a 100 MHz core and 1.43 ms on a 1 GHz core.Cross-platform validation confirms deployment readiness across QEMU virt, VisionFive2, and HiFive Unmatched platforms, with deterministic execution and full UART traceability. Security analysis demonstrates 128-bit IND-CCA quantum resistance with tamper-evident logging and constant-time Dilithium2 via masked pqm4 integration. The crypto-agile design supports future PQC migration (Falcon, SPHINCS+) while maintaining a sub-100 kB footprint suitable for resource-constrained embedded deployment. PQBoot-C provides the first open-source, QEMU-reproducible baseline for post-quantum RISC-V secure boot, bridging the critical research-to-deployment gap.

title: A new approach to rating scale definition with quantum-inspired optimization
abstract: In finance, assessing the creditworthiness of loan applicants requires lenders to cluster borrowers using rating scales. Financial institutions must define the scales in compliance with strict institutional constraints, resulting in solving a complex combinatorial constrained optimization problem. This contribution studies how to solve this problem using a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model, a formulation suitable for quantum hardware. We validate this approach by testing the proposed formulation with classical heuristics. We then benchmark the results against a brute-force method to demonstrate consistent solution quality and highlight the framework's suitability for more complex scenarios.

title: GeoGuide: Hierarchical Geometric Guidance for Open-Vocabulary 3D Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D semantic segmentation aims to segment arbitrary categories beyond the training set. Existing methods predominantly rely on distilling knowledge from 2D open-vocabulary models. However, aligning 3D features to the 2D representation space restricts intrinsic 3D geometric learning and inherits errors from 2D predictions. To address these limitations, we propose GeoGuide, a novel framework that leverages pretrained 3D models to integrate hierarchical geometry-semantic consistency for open-vocabulary 3D segmentation. Specifically, we introduce an Uncertainty-based Superpoint Distillation module to fuse geometric and semantic features for estimating per-point uncertainty, adaptively weighting 2D features within superpoints to suppress noise while preserving discriminative information to enhance local semantic consistency. Furthermore, our Instance-level Mask Reconstruction module leverages geometric priors to enforce semantic consistency within instances by reconstructing complete instance masks. Additionally, our Inter-Instance Relation Consistency module aligns geometric and semantic similarity matrices to calibrate cross-instance consistency for same-category objects, mitigating viewpoint-induced semantic drift. Extensive experiments on ScanNet v2, Matterport3D, and nuScenes demonstrate the superior performance of GeoGuide.

title: Adversarial Bandit Optimization with Globally Bounded Perturbations to Linear Losses
abstract: We study a class of adversarial bandit optimization problems in which the loss functions may be non-convex and non-smooth. In each round, the learner observes a loss that consists of an underlying linear component together with an additional perturbation applied after the learner selects an action. The perturbations are measured relative to the linear losses and are constrained by a global budget that bounds their cumulative magnitude over time. Under this model, we establish both expected and high-probability regret guarantees. As a special case of our analysis, we recover an improved high-probability regret bound for classical bandit linear optimization, which corresponds to the setting without perturbations. We further complement our upper bounds by proving a lower bound on the expected regret.

title: Human-AI Co-authoring for Personalized Practice With Multilayer Graph
abstract: This paper presents a proof-of-concept for a scalable approach to personalized learning that generates practice questions aligned to intended practice targets, controlling for question complexity. The focus is to provide learner-centered scaffolding in preparation for assessments by generating questions that align learner topic proficiency with targeted complexity. Historical assessment items are transformed into a topic-linked representation by multi-labeling each question with topics from a predefined syllabus. The labeling is produced by employing a previously built prompt-engineered GPT-5 model configuration with retrieval augmented generation. Topic labels are combined with student performance traces to derive personalized topic-level proficiency proxies. We then build a multilayer graph based on conceptual hierarchy and historical co-assessment. Querying the multilayer graph retrieves coherent topic sets around a student's priority topics based on learning needs, supporting content selection that is both topically consistent and conceptually coherent. A prompt-engineered GPT-5 model then generates questions for an inferred SOLO taxonomy level based on a learner's profile (proficiency and residue), conditioned on the retrieved topic sets. Outputs are evaluated for SOLO alignment and profile calibration through expert review, showing a high level of agreement. This methodology offers a pathway to operationalizing human-AI collaboration for adaptive practice, enabling scalable, varied revision for learners.

title: Research on Student Psychological Analysis Method Based on Particle Swarm Optimization and K-means Clustering Algorithm
abstract: Traditional student psychological analysis methods exhibit significant shortcomings, characterized by high subjectivity and insufficient clustering accuracy and global optimization capabilities. To address these issues, this paper proposes a student psychological analysis solution integrating Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and K-means clustering. University students were selected as research subjects, with core psychological indicators collected and standardized to construct a dataset. To mitigate the deficiency of K-means' random initial cluster center selection, the PSO algorithm was introduced to optimize this key parameter. By combining Euclidean distance, the clustering similarity measurement method was improved, resulting in a PSO-K-means hybrid algorithm. Comparative experiments validated the algorithm's practical effectiveness, employing multiple evaluation metrics to assess its performance. The results demonstrate that this hybrid algorithm can accurately classify student psychological states, providing reliable technical support for psychological intervention efforts in universities.

title: Anomaly Detection for Circuit Waveforms Using Diffusion Model
abstract: Circuit waveform inspection is critical to ensuring performance and reliability in consumer electronic products. However, engineers in industrial production lines often inspect waveforms manually, requiring technical expertise and time. To automate and speed up testing, we propose a diffusion model based normal waveform generator (DNWG) that reconstructs waveform images using only normal data, eliminating abnormal sample collection and retraining for unknown anomalies. By integrating masking techniques to preserve output accuracy, DNWG enables anomaly detection for previously unseen issues. In addition, we introduce the compositional similarity index, which considers the electrical and physical properties of circuits, improving upon conventional similarity metrics. This approach increases efficiency for anomaly detection in circuit waveform inspection.

title: Novel Machine Learning and Quantum Computing for Audio Biometrics: Deep Audio Feature Analysis and Speech Patterns for Real-Time Authentication Systems
abstract: Biometric authentication is essential for secure identity management in the age of digital services and ecosystems. Audio-based authentication outperforms other biometric methods due to its ease of use and compatibility with most devices. Most audio biometric systems have background noise, deception, and real-time use. A new quantum computing-ML architecture improves deep audio feature analysis and speech pattern recognition for real-time authentication systems. Deep learning and quantum physics provide accurate, high-dimensional speech data representations. Recurrent and convolutional neural networks identify audio patterns. We can adjust to various expressions since we can focus on one task. Quantum kernel estimation and variational quantum circuits trump basic machine learning. They protect the system from outside influences and threats, enabling its widespread acceptance. Edge computing lets lowresource devices learn and judge quickly, enabling real-time authentication. Quantum anomaly detection reduces replay attacks, vocal changes, and deepfake speech. Real and virtual acoustic testing have deeper accuracy, FAR, and FRR. A novel audio authentication biometrics solution uses machine learning and quantum computing. The findings show that query language and machine learning frameworks can overcome security, robustness, and scalability challenges. Voice interfaces and audio-driven technology are growing in consumer electronics, finance, and infrastructure. Safe, effective, and future-proof identity verification is achieved with this method.

title: Quantum-Inspired approaches to Multi-robot Scheduling and Control using QAOA and VQE
abstract: Quantum computation injection into robot automation opens up new avenues for boosting multi-robot complicated task scheduling and real-time adaptive control. Conventional optimization methods barely keep up with the challenges of scalability and efficiency in dynamic environments, thus becoming one of the bottlenecks for successful robotic coordination. This paper puts forward two leading quantum algorithms, Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and Variational Quantum Eigen solver (VQE), as a remedy to these shortcomings. Through the use of quantum parallelism and hybrid quantum-classical architectures, the intended solution is to elevate task assignment effectiveness and interactive response capacity in multi-robotic systems. Among other things, the proposed work aims at setting up a quantum inspired optimization model to schedule a task, an adaptive and real-time decision-support control framework, and the experimental demonstration of the algorithm's capability to handle complexity and high volume in robotic environments. Computer-based simulations alongside actual experiments, as a matter of fact, will be able to outperform regular optimizations, hence proving the transformative potentials of quantum algorithms on robotic automation.

title: Learnable Quantum Efficiency Filters for Urban Hyperspectral Segmentation
abstract: Hyperspectral sensing provides rich spectral information for scene understanding in urban driving, but its high dimensionality poses challenges for interpretation and efficient learning. We introduce Learnable Quantum Efficiency (LQE), a physics-inspired, interpretable dimensionality reduction (DR) method that parameterizes smooth high-order spectral response functions that emulate plausible sensor quantum efficiency curves. Unlike conventional methods or unconstrained learnable layers, LQE enforces physically motivated constraints, including a single dominant peak, smooth responses, and bounded bandwidth. This formulation yields a compact spectral representation that preserves discriminative information while remaining fully differentiable and end-to-end trainable within semantic segmentation models (SSMs). We conduct systematic evaluations across three publicly available multi-class hyperspectral urban driving datasets, comparing LQE against six conventional and seven learnable baseline DR methods across six SSMs. Averaged across all SSMs and configurations, LQE achieves the highest average mIoU, improving over conventional methods by 2.45\%, 0.45\%, and 1.04\%, and over learnable methods by 1.18\%, 1.56\%, and 0.81\% on HyKo, HSI-Drive, and Hyperspectral City, respectively. LQE maintains strong parameter efficiency (12--36 parameters compared to 51--22K for competing learnable approaches) and competitive inference latency. Ablation studies show that low-order configurations are optimal, while the learned spectral filters converge to dataset-intrinsic wavelength patterns. These results demonstrate that physics-informed spectral learning can improve both performance and interpretability, providing a principled bridge between hyperspectral perception and data-driven multispectral sensor design for automotive vision systems.

evidence.title: Learnable Quantum Efficiency Filters for Urban Hyperspectral Segmentation
evidence.abstract: Hyperspectral sensing provides rich spectral information for scene understanding in urban driving, but its high dimensionality poses challenges for interpretation and efficient learning. We introduce Learnable Quantum Efficiency (LQE), a physics-inspired, interpretable dimensionality reduction (DR) method that parameterizes smooth high-order spectral response functions that emulate plausible sensor quantum efficiency curves. Unlike conventional methods or unconstrained learnable layers, LQE enforces physically motivated constraints, including a single dominant peak, smooth responses, and bounded bandwidth. This formulation yields a compact spectral representation that preserves discriminative information while remaining fully differentiable and end-to-end trainable within semantic segmentation models (SSMs). We conduct systematic evaluations across three publicly available multi-class hyperspectral urban driving datasets, comparing LQE against six conventional and seven learnable baseline DR methods across six SSMs. Averaged across all SSMs and configurations, LQE achieves the highest average mIoU, improving over conventional methods by 2.45\%, 0.45\%, and 1.04\%, and over learnable methods by 1.18\%, 1.56\%, and 0.81\% on HyKo, HSI-Drive, and Hyperspectral City, respectively. LQE maintains strong parameter efficiency (12--36 parameters compared to 51--22K for competing learnable approaches) and competitive inference latency. Ablation studies show that low-order configurations are optimal, while the learned spectral filters converge to dataset-intrinsic wavelength patterns. These results demonstrate that physics-informed spectral learning can improve both performance and interpretability, providing a principled bridge between hyperspectral perception and data-driven multispectral sensor design for automotive vision systems.

title: Improved Approximation Algorithms and Hardness Results for Shortest Common Superstring with Reverse Complements
abstract: The Shortest Common Superstring (SCS) problem is a fundamental task in sequence analysis. In genome assembly, however, the double-stranded nature of DNA implies that each fragment may occur either in its original orientation or as its reverse complement. This motivates the Shortest Common Superstring with Reverse Complements (SCS-RC) problem, which asks for a shortest string that contains, for each input string, either the string itself or its reverse complement as a substring. The previously best-known approximation ratio for SCS-RC was $\frac{23}{8}$. In this paper, we present a new approximation algorithm achieving an improved ratio of $\frac{8}{3}$. Our approach computes an optimal constrained cycle cover by reducing the problem, via a novel gadget construction, to a maximum-weight perfect matching in a general graph. We also investigate the computational hardness of SCS-RC. While the decision version is known to be NP-complete, no explicit inapproximability results were previously established. We show that the hardness of SCS carries over to SCS-RC through a polynomial-time reduction, implying that it is NP-hard to approximate SCS-RC within a factor better than $\frac{333}{332}$. Notably, this hardness result holds even for the DNA alphabet.

title: Reasoning About the Non-Existent in Large Language Models: Benchmark Success, Negation Failure, and Exploratory Creativity
abstract: Can artificial intelligence reason about things that do not exist, are not true, or are merely hypothetical? This paper addresses these questions with a two-part analysis of non-existence reasoning in state-of-the-art large language models. The analysis includes four components: counterfactual inference, negation handling, creative novelty, and multi-turn persistence of imaginary knowledge. Part 1 uses a benchmark-calibrated forecasting model to predict future performance for 12 models on 15,300 simulated datapoints. Part 2 revisits the question with live API evaluations of 5 state-of-the-art models on over 654 items covering CRASS-style counterfactual questions, negation tasks, creativity prompts, and multi-turn dialogues about imaginary topics. The outcome is a differentiated capability profile rather than a simple yes or no answer to the question of whether AI can reason about non-existence. The sampled CRASS items produced near-ceiling performance relative to the published human baseline, suggesting that some portions of the benchmark may no longer provide strong discriminative power among state-of-the-art models. By contrast, negation was associated with statistically significant performance drops in the four complete model runs, with the same directional tendency also visible in the partial fifth run. The conclusions about creative novelty and multi-turn imaginary persistence are more provisional since they rested on proxy measures and heuristic contradiction detection. In substance, the results imply that top models can execute certain types of structured counterfactual reasoning effectively but display a robust and replicable deficit with respect to negation; indications of difficulty with creative novelty and multi-turn imaginative persistence are present but rest on weaker proxy measures and should be treated as provisional. In method, they underscore the importance of treating benchmark-calibrated forecasts as perishable hypotheses that must be revalidated with live model evaluations in a rapidly evolving LLM environment.

title: 【民間航空会社向け Geometric Intelligence理論導入支援資料】偏西風の逆関数
abstract: 本書の位置づけ 本書は『ジオメトリック・インテリジェンス』理論(第1巻・第2巻。以下、GIと記す)の使用方法を解説するためのケース・スタディ資料(物語形式)である。2026年3月現在、実在する数学の定理と人工知能技術、暗号技術及びIT技術のみを用いている。 ジオメトリック・インテリジェンス(1巻目) https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19140918 https://zenn.dev/etalecohomology/books/3761995ca27127 ジオメトリック・インテリジェンス(2巻目) https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19157891 ケース・スタディ資料(物語形式)は、どの業界の企業経営に適用するのかによって、工夫すべき点が業界ごとに異なる。とくに、入力データの収集とデータ間の関係の調整(名寄せ・時系列の粒度や分類の粒度の共通化、単位の異なるデータを比較可能にするための統計的な標準化など)は、それぞれの業界ごとに、データセットの特徴が大きく異なることから、業界の違いを越えた画一的なデータ前処理工程の王道は存在しない。そのため、各業界別に、ケース・スタディ資料を作成する方針を取っている。 このガイドブックは、民間航空会社を取り扱っている(これまでのシリーズでは、繊維製造メーカー企業、ゼネコン企業、半導体製造企業を対象とした『ジオメトリック・インテリジェンス』導入解説を行ってきた)。 ストーリーの概要と本書の設定を選んだ理由 舞台は2031年。日本の国家安全保障局(NSS)から天翔航空に対し、特定の外交的貨物を72時間以内にロンドン・ヒースロー空港まで輸送するよう要請が下る。しかし、①ロシアのウクライナ侵攻以来続くシベリア上空の閉鎖(欧米・日本・カナダの航空会社に対する報復的なOverflight Permit撤回)、②台湾海峡をめぐる緊張による中国FIRの段階的な通過制限強化、③フーシ派(イエメン武装勢力)による紅海沿岸の対空ミサイル・ドローン脅威——という三つの独立した禁止区域が、東京・ロンドン間のいかなる通常航路も遮断していた。残された選択肢は、北極海を経由する非標準航路のみであった。 この設定は、現在進行中の地政学的リスクを忠実に反映している。1944年のシカゴ条約第1条は「各国はその領土の上空において完全かつ排他的な主権を有する」と定め、第9条は緊急時に即座の飛行禁止措置を認める。制度の枠組みは80年近く変わっていないが、①この主権を行使する主体の多様化(国家から非国家主体であるフーシ派まで)、②政治的報復手段としての領空閉鎖の常態化、③国際条約の外側から来る非対称な脅威の出現——という三重の変化が重なり、民間航空会社が運航継続のために直面する制約の複雑さは質的に変容した。 本書は、この複雑さを「飛行可能な空域全体を底空間Bとしたとき、三つの独立した禁止区域が底空間に三つの穴を開け、第1コホモロジー群H¹(B, F)が非自明となる」という位相幾何学の言語で正確に記述し、それを数学的に解く物語として構成されている。地政学的リスクを、現場の意思決定者が運用できる数学的枠組みへと橋渡しすることが、本書の中心的な問いである。 GI理論を民間航空便の運航に適用する場合の特徴 航空データセットの特性——他産業との比較 航空業界のデータセットが他産業と異なる最大の特徴は、風(ジェット気流)が計量そのものを非対称にするという点にある。製造業や海運業では、環境要因は外生的なノイズとして扱える場合が多い。しかし航空では、同一区間を東方向に飛ぶ場合と西方向に飛ぶ場合とで飛行時間が2〜3時間異なる。これは「距離」の概念が対称性を失うことを意味しており、標準的なリーマン計量(方向非依存の距離)では現実を正確に記述できない。 本書で用いたのはフィンスラー計量のランダー型F = α + β(Randers metric)である。αは背景のリーマン計量(風のない場合の距離)、βはジェット気流を表す1-形式(飛行方向に応じて符号が変わる非対称な補正項)であり、その和Fが「風の中を飛ぶ航空機の実際の距離感覚」を記述する。ランダー計量はツェルメロの航法問題(風の中での最適航法の数学的定式化)と等価であることが証明されており、航空運航の物理を最も自然に記述する計量クラスである。 また、航空データは**ADS-B(Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast)**という、航空機自身がGPSから計算した位置・速度・高度を1090MHz帯で自動送信するシステムによって継続的に蓄積されている。本書では東京発ロンドン着の過去5年分の全フライト(23,847件)のADS-Bデータを使用した。製造業の生産ラインデータや海運の航行ログとは異なり、このデータには「風速ベクトルの直接観測値」が内包されている:真対気速度(TAS)と対地速度(GS)の差分が、そのままβ項の推定値となる。これは他産業にはない航空データ特有の性質であり、外生的な気象予報に頼ることなく、実フライトデータそのものから計量を学習できる。 GI理論の三条件(命題1.1)を航空データで充足するための工夫 GI Vol.1 命題1.1は、VAE(変分自己符号化器)から可微分多様体を構築するために以下の三条件を要求する。 条件(i):VAEデコーダのC³級滑らかさ 活性化関数の選択が鍵となる。航空多様体では高度・速度・位置の急激な変化を扱うため、ReLU(折れ曲がり点で1階微分が不連続)は使用できない。全層にtanh(双曲線正接関数、C∞級)を使用することで、測地線方程式が要求するクリストッフェル記号の計算に必要な2階微分の連続性を保証した。 条件(ii):ヤコビ行列のフルランク VAE訓練後にデコーダのヤコビ行列のSVD(特異値分解)を実施し、最小特異値0.312(ゼロから十分離れている)を確認した。また、KNN(k近傍)保存率0.891(目標値0.85以上)により、潜在空間の幾何学が実フライトデータの多様体構造を忠実に反映していることを検証した。 条件(iii):ランダー条件 ‖β‖_α < 1 この条件は「風速が航空機の真対気速度を超えない」という物理的条件と等価である。787-9のTAS(約250 m/s、マッハ0.85)に対し、北太平洋のジェット気流は典型的に50〜100 m/s(最大値で約0.40の比率)であり、条件は全区間で満たされた。実測値は出発時0.38、飛行中最大0.56であった。なお、0.65を超えると時変フィンスラー計量の理論的安定性が保証されなくなることから、超過時にはリーマン計量へのフォールバックを設計段階から組み込んだ。この「理論の限界を正直に設計する」姿勢は、航空安全(DO-178C)との整合性の観点からも不可欠である。 このほか、GFS・ECMWFの気象予報モデルとADS-Bの実測値を統合した二重データソース構造により、β項の推定誤差を±0.04以内に抑え、通信途絶時でも機上Embodied Agentが最後の既知計量から局所的に更新を継続できるアーキテクチャを採用した。 本書の読者へのメッセージ 本書が描く世界では、一人のエンジニア(カイト)が「今まで数学と物理とプログラミングだけ学んできた。でも今回の一件に参加してから、国際政治と法律を本腰入れて学ばなきゃと思っている」と語る場面がある。これは、GI理論の実践者に求められる知識の横断性を象徴している。 航空運航にGI理論を適用するためには、以下が同時に必要である。 数学の知識——フィンスラー幾何学(ランダー計量・チャーン接続・測地線方程式)、位相幾何学(コホモロジー群、ジグザグ・パーシステンス)、最適制御理論(ポントリャーギンの最大原理・随伴変数)、情報幾何学(フィッシャー情報量計量・VAE引き戻し計量)が、互いに接続した一つの体系として使いこなせること。本書に登場する数学は、それぞれ独立した分野として一流大学の大学院レベルで教えられているが、それらを横断するカリキュラムは2026年現在、世界のどこにも存在しない。 コード実装とAIアルゴリズムの知見——VAEの訓練ループとC³条件を満たすアーキテクチャ設計、フィンスラー測地線の数値解法(約40秒で再計算できる実装)、14体のAI Agentの並列設計と通信プロトコル、形式検証ツール(Lean 4)とZKML(ゼロ知識証明による機械学習の計算検証)の組み合わせ。理論を「動く実装」に落とし込む工学的知見が不可欠である。 地政学と国際法の知識——シカゴ条約の条文、二国間航空協定の枠組み、非国家主体が生み出す法の外側のリスク、制裁リスト(OFAC・EU・国連)のリアルタイム監視。数学が設計した航路が「法的に飛べるか」を判断するためには、これらを数式と同じ精度で理解する必要がある。数学が地形を設計し、法律と国際政治がその地形の制約を決める。 判断力と勇気——本書の核心的な問いは「測地線を信じますか」という一言に集約される。数学的に最適な経路が存在すると証明されても、通信が途絶した北極海上空でロシア領空の12海里以内まで接近するか否かの最終判断は、機長が下す。AIは測地線を計算し、人間が決断する。理論の限界を正直に認識した上で、不完全な情報のもとで行動する意志——これが、GI理論の実践者に求められる最後の、そして最も重要な条件である。 GI理論は「一人の天才が全部わかる」ことを前提としない。数学者・エンジニア・パイロット・ディスパッチャー・アクチュアリー・地政学アナリストが、同じ数学的言語で対話できるチームを前提としている。本書は、そのチームがどのように機能するかの具体的な描写でもある。 なぜ航空業界にはGIを用いた統合リスク管理が不可欠なのか 航空業界が直面するリスクは、他産業と比較して以下の三点で構造的に異なる。 第一に、リスクの同時多発性と相互依存性。本書が描くように、気象リスク(ジェット気流の予報外れ)・運航安全リスク(ETOPSの制約)・地政学的リスク(FIRの閉鎖)・保険リスク(戦争リスク条項)・通信リスク(太陽フレアによる電離層障害)が12時間のフライト中に同時に発生し、かつ相互に依存する。ETOPS代替空港の気象悪化が保険ファイバーのH¹を変化させ、それがルート変更の可否に影響する。これらを個別に管理するサイロ型リスク管理は、構造的に破綻する。 第二に、リアルタイム性の要求。航空機は時速900 km で飛行している。地政学的な情勢変化(NOTAMによる空域制限の発出)から気象の急変まで、判断のサイクルタイムは分単位である。経営会議で半期に一度リスクを審議するような産業とは根本的に異なる。GI理論が採用する「測地線のリアルタイム再計算(約40秒)と14体のAI Agentによる並列監視」は、この要求に対応する設計である。 第三に、「通常の経路が存在しない」状況への対応。従来の航路最適化は「既存の航空路の中からどれを選ぶか」という選択問題を前提としてきた。しかし、地政学的緊張が高まり複数の大国が同時期に領空を閉鎖する現代では、既存のどの航空路も選択できない状況——本書でいうH¹(B, F) ≠ 0の状態——が現実のシナリオとして生じうる。この場合に必要なのは「新しい測地線を設計する数学」であり、従来のグリッド探索アルゴリズムでは対応できない。ランダー計量上の連続的な測地線方程式を解く能力は、まさにこの「通常の経路が存在しない」局面のためにある。 さらに、航空業界は乗客の生命安全という最高度の責任を負う。DO-178C(航空電子機器ソフトウェア安全基準)との整合、ETOPS認証要件、各国航空当局への説明責任——これらを充足しながらAIシステムを運航に組み込む際には、「数学的に正しいことと、航空安全として正しいことは別の概念」(本書第15章、CTO ヨルゲンの言葉)という緊張を常に意識する必要がある。ZKMLによる計算の形式検証と、パイロットの最終判断権限の明示的な保持が、この緊張を解消する設計原則となる。 GI Ver.3への展望 本書(GIケーススタディ第11作、航空産業編)は、GI Vol.3の数学的素材を先取りする形で設計されている。 GI Vol.1(リーマン計量・フィンスラー計量・H¹コホモロジー・VAE引き戻し計量)とGI Vol.2(シンプレクティック幾何・ワイル幾何・ジグザグ・パーシステンス・AI Agent設計)で確立した枠組みを、本書は航空という極限状況のもとで実証した。北太平洋でのリアルタイムβ項更新、北極海での通信途絶時11分間の自律運用、二つのコホモロジー問題の同時発生(ETOPS穴と保険穴)、極渦による計量急変時のリーマンへのフォールバックと時変フィンスラー計量の未解決問題——これらは、GI Vol.3が扱うべき数学的課題を実データから照射している。 GI Vol.3では次の数学領域の統合を予定している:シンプレクティック積分法の長期安定シミュレーションへの応用(エネルギー保存と構造保存)、ワイル幾何のゲージ不変性をAI出力検証に適用するフレームワーク、情報幾何学(フィッシャー情報量計量)によるSIGINT異常検知との接続、最適輸送理論(ワッサースタイン計量)による確率分布の時間変化追跡、双曲幾何(ポアンカレ埋め込み)による組織・ネットワーク構造の表現。 本書の後日談(第16章)では、天翔航空の航空多様体と曙海運の海上多様体の統合構想——海と空が同じ数学的言語で動く日本発の地理情報多様体インフラ——が語られる。これがGIケーススタディ第12作(海運産業編)へと引き継がれ、GI Vol.3の理論的裏付けとなる予定である。 GI理論が目指すのは「数学と、法律と、地政学と、工学が交差する場所に立てる人間が設計するシステム」である。その交差点は、2026年現在、世界のどの大学のカリキュラムにも存在しない。本ケーススタディシリーズが、その交差点を実践の場から構築するための素材となることを期待する。

evidence.title: 【民間航空会社向け Geometric Intelligence理論導入支援資料】偏西風の逆関数
evidence.abstract: 本書の位置づけ 本書は『ジオメトリック・インテリジェンス』理論(第1巻・第2巻。以下、GIと記す)の使用方法を解説するためのケース・スタディ資料(物語形式)である。2026年3月現在、実在する数学の定理と人工知能技術、暗号技術及びIT技術のみを用いている。 ジオメトリック・インテリジェンス(1巻目) https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19140918 https://zenn.dev/etalecohomology/books/3761995ca27127 ジオメトリック・インテリジェンス(2巻目) https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19157891 ケース・スタディ資料(物語形式)は、どの業界の企業経営に適用するのかによって、工夫すべき点が業界ごとに異なる。とくに、入力データの収集とデータ間の関係の調整(名寄せ・時系列の粒度や分類の粒度の共通化、単位の異なるデータを比較可能にするための統計的な標準化など)は、それぞれの業界ごとに、データセットの特徴が大きく異なることから、業界の違いを越えた画一的なデータ前処理工程の王道は存在しない。そのため、各業界別に、ケース・スタディ資料を作成する方針を取っている。 このガイドブックは、民間航空会社を取り扱っている(これまでのシリーズでは、繊維製造メーカー企業、ゼネコン企業、半導体製造企業を対象とした『ジオメトリック・インテリジェンス』導入解説を行ってきた)。 ストーリーの概要と本書の設定を選んだ理由 舞台は2031年。日本の国家安全保障局(NSS)から天翔航空に対し、特定の外交的貨物を72時間以内にロンドン・ヒースロー空港まで輸送するよう要請が下る。しかし、①ロシアのウクライナ侵攻以来続くシベリア上空の閉鎖(欧米・日本・カナダの航空会社に対する報復的なOverflight Permit撤回)、②台湾海峡をめぐる緊張による中国FIRの段階的な通過制限強化、③フーシ派(イエメン武装勢力)による紅海沿岸の対空ミサイル・ドローン脅威——という三つの独立した禁止区域が、東京・ロンドン間のいかなる通常航路も遮断していた。残された選択肢は、北極海を経由する非標準航路のみであった。 この設定は、現在進行中の地政学的リスクを忠実に反映している。1944年のシカゴ条約第1条は「各国はその領土の上空において完全かつ排他的な主権を有する」と定め、第9条は緊急時に即座の飛行禁止措置を認める。制度の枠組みは80年近く変わっていないが、①この主権を行使する主体の多様化(国家から非国家主体であるフーシ派まで)、②政治的報復手段としての領空閉鎖の常態化、③国際条約の外側から来る非対称な脅威の出現——という三重の変化が重なり、民間航空会社が運航継続のために直面する制約の複雑さは質的に変容した。 本書は、この複雑さを「飛行可能な空域全体を底空間Bとしたとき、三つの独立した禁止区域が底空間に三つの穴を開け、第1コホモロジー群H¹(B, F)が非自明となる」という位相幾何学の言語で正確に記述し、それを数学的に解く物語として構成されている。地政学的リスクを、現場の意思決定者が運用できる数学的枠組みへと橋渡しすることが、本書の中心的な問いである。 GI理論を民間航空便の運航に適用する場合の特徴 航空データセットの特性——他産業との比較 航空業界のデータセットが他産業と異なる最大の特徴は、風(ジェット気流)が計量そのものを非対称にするという点にある。製造業や海運業では、環境要因は外生的なノイズとして扱える場合が多い。しかし航空では、同一区間を東方向に飛ぶ場合と西方向に飛ぶ場合とで飛行時間が2〜3時間異なる。これは「距離」の概念が対称性を失うことを意味しており、標準的なリーマン計量(方向非依存の距離)では現実を正確に記述できない。 本書で用いたのはフィンスラー計量のランダー型F = α + β(Randers metric)である。αは背景のリーマン計量(風のない場合の距離)、βはジェット気流を表す1-形式(飛行方向に応じて符号が変わる非対称な補正項)であり、その和Fが「風の中を飛ぶ航空機の実際の距離感覚」を記述する。ランダー計量はツェルメロの航法問題(風の中での最適航法の数学的定式化)と等価であることが証明されており、航空運航の物理を最も自然に記述する計量クラスである。 また、航空データは**ADS-B(Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast)**という、航空機自身がGPSから計算した位置・速度・高度を1090MHz帯で自動送信するシステムによって継続的に蓄積されている。本書では東京発ロンドン着の過去5年分の全フライト(23,847件)のADS-Bデータを使用した。製造業の生産ラインデータや海運の航行ログとは異なり、このデータには「風速ベクトルの直接観測値」が内包されている:真対気速度(TAS)と対地速度(GS)の差分が、そのままβ項の推定値となる。これは他産業にはない航空データ特有の性質であり、外生的な気象予報に頼ることなく、実フライトデータそのものから計量を学習できる。 GI理論の三条件(命題1.1)を航空データで充足するための工夫 GI Vol.1 命題1.1は、VAE(変分自己符号化器)から可微分多様体を構築するために以下の三条件を要求する。 条件(i):VAEデコーダのC³級滑らかさ 活性化関数の選択が鍵となる。航空多様体では高度・速度・位置の急激な変化を扱うため、ReLU(折れ曲がり点で1階微分が不連続)は使用できない。全層にtanh(双曲線正接関数、C∞級)を使用することで、測地線方程式が要求するクリストッフェル記号の計算に必要な2階微分の連続性を保証した。 条件(ii):ヤコビ行列のフルランク VAE訓練後にデコーダのヤコビ行列のSVD(特異値分解)を実施し、最小特異値0.312(ゼロから十分離れている)を確認した。また、KNN(k近傍)保存率0.891(目標値0.85以上)により、潜在空間の幾何学が実フライトデータの多様体構造を忠実に反映していることを検証した。 条件(iii):ランダー条件 ‖β‖_α < 1 この条件は「風速が航空機の真対気速度を超えない」という物理的条件と等価である。787-9のTAS(約250 m/s、マッハ0.85)に対し、北太平洋のジェット気流は典型的に50〜100 m/s(最大値で約0.40の比率)であり、条件は全区間で満たされた。実測値は出発時0.38、飛行中最大0.56であった。なお、0.65を超えると時変フィンスラー計量の理論的安定性が保証されなくなることから、超過時にはリーマン計量へのフォールバックを設計段階から組み込んだ。この「理論の限界を正直に設計する」姿勢は、航空安全(DO-178C)との整合性の観点からも不可欠である。 このほか、GFS・ECMWFの気象予報モデルとADS-Bの実測値を統合した二重データソース構造により、β項の推定誤差を±0.04以内に抑え、通信途絶時でも機上Embodied Agentが最後の既知計量から局所的に更新を継続できるアーキテクチャを採用した。 本書の読者へのメッセージ 本書が描く世界では、一人のエンジニア(カイト)が「今まで数学と物理とプログラミングだけ学んできた。でも今回の一件に参加してから、国際政治と法律を本腰入れて学ばなきゃと思っている」と語る場面がある。これは、GI理論の実践者に求められる知識の横断性を象徴している。 航空運航にGI理論を適用するためには、以下が同時に必要である。 数学の知識——フィンスラー幾何学(ランダー計量・チャーン接続・測地線方程式)、位相幾何学(コホモロジー群、ジグザグ・パーシステンス)、最適制御理論(ポントリャーギンの最大原理・随伴変数)、情報幾何学(フィッシャー情報量計量・VAE引き戻し計量)が、互いに接続した一つの体系として使いこなせること。本書に登場する数学は、それぞれ独立した分野として一流大学の大学院レベルで教えられているが、それらを横断するカリキュラムは2026年現在、世界のどこにも存在しない。 コード実装とAIアルゴリズムの知見——VAEの訓練ループとC³条件を満たすアーキテクチャ設計、フィンスラー測地線の数値解法(約40秒で再計算できる実装)、14体のAI Agentの並列設計と通信プロトコル、形式検証ツール(Lean 4)とZKML(ゼロ知識証明による機械学習の計算検証)の組み合わせ。理論を「動く実装」に落とし込む工学的知見が不可欠である。 地政学と国際法の知識——シカゴ条約の条文、二国間航空協定の枠組み、非国家主体が生み出す法の外側のリスク、制裁リスト(OFAC・EU・国連)のリアルタイム監視。数学が設計した航路が「法的に飛べるか」を判断するためには、これらを数式と同じ精度で理解する必要がある。数学が地形を設計し、法律と国際政治がその地形の制約を決める。 判断力と勇気——本書の核心的な問いは「測地線を信じますか」という一言に集約される。数学的に最適な経路が存在すると証明されても、通信が途絶した北極海上空でロシア領空の12海里以内まで接近するか否かの最終判断は、機長が下す。AIは測地線を計算し、人間が決断する。理論の限界を正直に認識した上で、不完全な情報のもとで行動する意志——これが、GI理論の実践者に求められる最後の、そして最も重要な条件である。 GI理論は「一人の天才が全部わかる」ことを前提としない。数学者・エンジニア・パイロット・ディスパッチャー・アクチュアリー・地政学アナリストが、同じ数学的言語で対話できるチームを前提としている。本書は、そのチームがどのように機能するかの具体的な描写でもある。 なぜ航空業界にはGIを用いた統合リスク管理が不可欠なのか 航空業界が直面するリスクは、他産業と比較して以下の三点で構造的に異なる。 第一に、リスクの同時多発性と相互依存性。本書が描くように、気象リスク(ジェット気流の予報外れ)・運航安全リスク(ETOPSの制約)・地政学的リスク(FIRの閉鎖)・保険リスク(戦争リスク条項)・通信リスク(太陽フレアによる電離層障害)が12時間のフライト中に同時に発生し、かつ相互に依存する。ETOPS代替空港の気象悪化が保険ファイバーのH¹を変化させ、それがルート変更の可否に影響する。これらを個別に管理するサイロ型リスク管理は、構造的に破綻する。 第二に、リアルタイム性の要求。航空機は時速900 km で飛行している。地政学的な情勢変化(NOTAMによる空域制限の発出)から気象の急変まで、判断のサイクルタイムは分単位である。経営会議で半期に一度リスクを審議するような産業とは根本的に異なる。GI理論が採用する「測地線のリアルタイム再計算(約40秒)と14体のAI Agentによる並列監視」は、この要求に対応する設計である。 第三に、「通常の経路が存在しない」状況への対応。従来の航路最適化は「既存の航空路の中からどれを選ぶか」という選択問題を前提としてきた。しかし、地政学的緊張が高まり複数の大国が同時期に領空を閉鎖する現代では、既存のどの航空路も選択できない状況——本書でいうH¹(B, F) ≠ 0の状態——が現実のシナリオとして生じうる。この場合に必要なのは「新しい測地線を設計する数学」であり、従来のグリッド探索アルゴリズムでは対応できない。ランダー計量上の連続的な測地線方程式を解く能力は、まさにこの「通常の経路が存在しない」局面のためにある。 さらに、航空業界は乗客の生命安全という最高度の責任を負う。DO-178C(航空電子機器ソフトウェア安全基準)との整合、ETOPS認証要件、各国航空当局への説明責任——これらを充足しながらAIシステムを運航に組み込む際には、「数学的に正しいことと、航空安全として正しいことは別の概念」(本書第15章、CTO ヨルゲンの言葉)という緊張を常に意識する必要がある。ZKMLによる計算の形式検証と、パイロットの最終判断権限の明示的な保持が、この緊張を解消する設計原則となる。 GI Ver.3への展望 本書(GIケーススタディ第11作、航空産業編)は、GI Vol.3の数学的素材を先取りする形で設計されている。 GI Vol.1(リーマン計量・フィンスラー計量・H¹コホモロジー・VAE引き戻し計量)とGI Vol.2(シンプレクティック幾何・ワイル幾何・ジグザグ・パーシステンス・AI Agent設計)で確立した枠組みを、本書は航空という極限状況のもとで実証した。北太平洋でのリアルタイムβ項更新、北極海での通信途絶時11分間の自律運用、二つのコホモロジー問題の同時発生(ETOPS穴と保険穴)、極渦による計量急変時のリーマンへのフォールバックと時変フィンスラー計量の未解決問題——これらは、GI Vol.3が扱うべき数学的課題を実データから照射している。 GI Vol.3では次の数学領域の統合を予定している:シンプレクティック積分法の長期安定シミュレーションへの応用(エネルギー保存と構造保存)、ワイル幾何のゲージ不変性をAI出力検証に適用するフレームワーク、情報幾何学(フィッシャー情報量計量)によるSIGINT異常検知との接続、最適輸送理論(ワッサースタイン計量)による確率分布の時間変化追跡、双曲幾何(ポアンカレ埋め込み)による組織・ネットワーク構造の表現。 title: Headlines You Won't Forget: Can Pronoun Insertion Increase Memorability?
abstract: For unrestricted data access, please go to the newest version of this dataset. This is the data repository for the CMCL 2026 paper "Headlines You Won't Forget: Can Pronoun Insertion Increase Memorability?" The zip-file "LLM revisions and Annotations" contains three files: annotation_samples.json and annotation_samples_2.json contain all LLM-revisions.annotations_of_LLM_revisions.json contains the non-aggregated annotation data for all LLM-revisions. Annotations for accuracy_subclass are ordered as follows: [misrepresentation, omission, addition]. Annotations for style subclass are ordered as [grammar, awkward style, inconsistent]. In the zip-file "Memory Experiment Data", we provide non-aggregated results of the memory experiment (experiment_data.json), as well as the recalled items matched to their respective headline id's (headline_items_matched). headlines.json provides information about the revision type, and group assignment of headline items. We further provide aggregated results in csv-files. Files for each study are provided in separate sub-directories. If you use this dataset in your research please cite the paper.

title: Pretrained Models and Reproducibility Archive for "From Characters to Syntax: Characterizing the Accuracy–Robustness Trade-off in Cross-Domain Authorship Verification"
abstract: This repository contains the pretrained model weights, vectorizer pipelines, and ablation study checkpoints for the paper "From Characters to Syntax: Characterizing the Accuracy–Robustness Trade-off in Cross-Domain Authorship Verification". The provided models were trained and evaluated across three distinct text domains (fanfiction, personal blogs, and corporate emails) to investigate the fundamental vulnerability of stylometric systems against semantic-preserving paraphrase attacks. Contents of this archive: Robust Siamese: The best-performing cross-domain model utilizing character n-gram features (includes .pth weights, vectorizer.pkl , and scaler.pkl ). Cross-Domain (CD) Siamese: The baseline generalist character 4-gram model trained across all domains. Robust DANN (Domain-Adversarial Neural Network): The multi-view syntactic feature model trained for high adversarial robustness. BERT Baseline: The contextual baseline model used for comparative evaluation. Syntactic Ablation Models: Pretrained checkpoints isolating Part-of-Speech (POS) trigrams, function word frequencies, and readability metrics to demonstrate the specific drivers of robustness in stylometric features. Usage: These weights are intended to be used directly with the PyTorch and Scikit-Learn inference pipelines provided in the official GitHub repository. Researchers can utilize this archive to perfectly reproduce the cross-domain accuracy (up to 86.2%) and attack success rate evaluations presented in the manuscript.

title: VentGuard: A Machine Learning-Based Real-Time Anomaly Detection and Early Warning System for Mechanical Ventilator Monitoring
abstract: Mechanical ventilation is a critical life-support intervention for patients with respiratory failure in intensive care units. However, timely detection of ventilator-related anomalies remains challenging due to the complexity of respiratory data streams. This paper presents VentGuard, a web-based platform that combines real-time data visualization with machine learning algorithms for automated anomaly detection in mechanical ventilator monitoring. Our system implements six unsupervised learning algorithms including Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, and DBSCAN, enabling comparative analysis and flexible model deployment. We propose a ML-enhanced detection approach that augments traditional rule-based clinical thresholds with machine learning pattern recognition. Experimental evaluation on 8,115 real-world ventilator records demonstrates that ML enhancement achieves 78-89% anomaly detection rates, providing consistent improvements of 3-10 percentage points over rule-based baseline methods, with Isolation Forest and One-Class SVM showing the most stable performance across varying training data volumes. The system’s modular architecture supports configurable training and real-time alert generation, making it suitable for deployment in critical care environments.

title: Design of Robotic Arm Control System Based on Fuzzy PID Algorithm
abstract: Addressing the nonlinear and strongly coupled characteristics of robotic manipulators, along with the poor robustness and limited adaptability of traditional PID control under complex operating conditions, this paper presents the designed of a robotic arm control system based on a fuzzy PID algorithm. Initially, the hardware of the robotic arm was divided into four core modules, clarifying the structure and collaborative logic of each component. Subsequently, a fuzzy PID controller is constructed, employing a six-step core process to achieve dynamic tuning of PID parameters. Finally, a simulation model of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) with load disturbance rejection is built using Matlab/Simulink to compare the control performance of traditional PID and fuzzy PID. The simulation results demonstrate that the fuzzy PID algorithm can reduce the three-phase current imbalance of the motor from 8.3% to 3.1%, significantly suppress torque and speed overshoot, substantially shorten disturbance recovery time, and limit steadystate fluctuations of the system to only$\mathbf{2 0 \%} \boldsymbol{\sim} \mathbf{2 5 \%}$of those observed with traditional PID. This algorithm effectively enhances the dynamic response speed and disturbance rejection capability of the robotic arm drive system, overcoming the limitations of traditional PID in nonlinear systems and providing a viable solution for optimizing control algorithms for robotic arms in high-end intelligent equipment.

title: LMDA: Lightweight Multiauthority CP-ABE Scheme Based on Dynamic Attributes for System Wide Information Management
abstract: The System Wide Information Management (SWIM) system serves as an advanced platform for managing and sharing diverse aviation data, such as aeronautical, flight, and meteorological information. With the exponential growth of aviation data, ensuring data security and privacy within SWIM has become increasingly important. Ciphertext-Policy Attribute-Based Encryption (CP-ABE) is widely regarded as an effective cryptographic technique for ensuring secure and private data access. However, traditional CP-ABE schemes rely on computationally expensive bilinear pairings, which are unsuitable for resource-constrained aviation Internet of Things application scenarios in SWIM, such as Aircraft Access to SWIM. To address this limitation, we propose a lightweight multi-authority CP-ABE scheme based on dynamic attributes. This scheme replaces bilinear pairing operations with efficient scalar multiplication on elliptic curve points and outsources most decryption operations to outsourcing decryption nodes, thereby significantly reducing computational overhead. In addition, this scheme introduces a dynamic attribute mechanism to support fine-grained access control, and outsources data verification and attribute revocation to the blockchain to ensure data integrity. Security analysis shows that our scheme achieves indistinguishability under adaptive chosen-ciphertext attacks and is resistant to collusion attacks. Experimental evaluations further demonstrate that our scheme significantly enhances computational and communication efficiency.

title: Reversible Quantum Digital Circuits and Quantum Random Number Generation Using Qiskit
abstract: Quantum computing requires logic operations to be implemented as reversible transformations. Classical combinational circuits must therefore be redesigned using reversible gate structures when mapped to quantum systems. In this work, fundamental quantum digital circuits are implemented using CNOT and Toffoli gates using the Qiskit framework.In addition, an 8-qubit Quantum Random Number Generator (QRNG) is developed and analyzed. Hadamard operations are applied to an 8-qubit register to produce a uniform superposition over 256 states. Measurement in the computational basis generates an 8-bit result per execution. By repeating the circuit 16 independent times and concatenation of the outputs produce a 128-bit random sequence. The QRNG is evaluated using Dirac notation, density operator representation and entropy analysis to verify uniform probability distribution under ideal simulation conditions.Simulation results confirm the correct logical functionality of the reversible arithmetic circuits and demonstrate high entropy random sequence generation using quantum measurement. The presented framework provides a structured approach for implementing digital logic and randomness generation in Qiskit.

title: Mastering AI Communication: The Art of Prompt Engineering
abstract: This chapter explains the four ingredients of a perfect prompt: be specific, give context, set boundaries, and choose the flavor. Common mistakes that kill the prompts include the “throw everything at the wall” approach; the “figure it out yourself” problem; and the “one size fits all” trap. Most clients actually appreciate the efficiency, as long as they are adding their own expertise and personal touch. The magic happens when they combine that efficiency with the skills, creativity, and understanding of what the clients actually need. When it comes to fact-checking with artificial intelligence (AI), one can use a few key strategies to ensure accuracy. For data, research, or client-facing reports that require complete accuracy, always supplement AI fact-check with a quick Google search or a trusted database. Prompt engineering is not about coding; it is about conversation.

title: Low-energy spectrum of double-junction superconducting circuits in the Born-Oppenheimer approximation
abstract: The superconductor-insulator-superconductor Josephson junction is the fundamental nonlinear element of superconducting circuits. Connecting two junctions in series gives rise to higher-harmonic content in the total energy-phase relation, enabling new design opportunities in multimode circuits. However, the double-junction element hosts an internal mode whose spectrum is set by the finite capacitances of the individual junctions. Using a Born-Oppenheimer approximation that treats the additional mode as fast compared to the qubit mode, we analyze the double-junction circuit element shunted by a large capacitor. Here, we derive an effective single-mode model of the qubit containing a correction term owing to the presence of the internal mode. In experimentally relevant parameter regimes, we numerically find that our model accurately describes the low-energy spectrum of the qubit. We further discuss how eliminating the internal degree of freedom affects the system's periodic boundary conditions and leads to non-uniqueness in performing the Born-Oppenheimer approximation. Finally, we analyze the harmonic content of the double-junction element and discuss its sensitivity to charge noise.

title: Hermes Seal: Zero-Knowledge Assurance for Autonomous Vehicle Communications
abstract: The application of zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) in autonomous systems is an emerging area of research, motivated by the growing need for regulatory compliance, transparent auditing, and trustworthy operation in decentralized environments. zk-SNARK is a powerful cryptographic tool that allows a party (the prover) to prove to another party (the verifier) that a statement about its own internal state is true, without revealing sensitive or proprietary data about that state. This paper proposes Hermes Seal: a zk-SNARK-based ZKP framework for enabling privacy-preserving, verifiable communication in vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) and vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) networks. The framework allows autonomous systems to generate cryptographic proofs of perception and decision-related computations without revealing proprietary models, sensor data, or internal system states, thereby supporting interoperability across heterogeneous autonomous systems. We present two real-world case studies implemented and empirically evaluated within our framework, demonstrating a step toward verifiable autonomous system information exchanges. The first demonstrates real-time proof generation and verification, achieving 8 ms proof generation and 1 ms verification on a GPU, while the second evaluates the performance of an autonomous vehicle perception stack, enabling proof of computation without exposing proprietary or confidential data. Furthermore, the framework can be integrated into AV perception stacks to facilitate verifiable interoperability and privacy-preserving cooperative perception. The demonstration code for this project is open source, available on Github.

title: ARTA: Adaptive Mixed-Resolution Token Allocation for Efficient Dense Feature Extraction
abstract: We present ARTA, a mixed-resolution coarse-to-fine vision transformer for efficient dense feature extraction. Unlike models that begin with dense high-resolution (fine) tokens, ARTA starts with low-resolution (coarse) tokens and uses a lightweight allocator to predict which regions require more fine tokens. The allocator iteratively predicts a semantic (class) boundary score and allocates additional tokens to patches above a low threshold, concentrating token density near boundaries while maintaining high sensitivity to weak boundary evidence. This targeted allocation encourages tokens to represent a single semantic class rather than a mixture of classes. Mixed-resolution attention enables interaction between coarse and fine tokens, focusing computation on semantically complex areas while avoiding redundant processing in homogeneous regions. Experiments demonstrate that ARTA achieves state-of-the-art results on ADE20K and COCO-Stuff with substantially fewer FLOPs, and delivers competitive performance on Cityscapes at markedly lower compute. For example, ARTA-Base attains 54.6 mIoU on ADE20K in the ~100M-parameter class while using fewer FLOPs and less memory than comparable backbones.

title: MuDD: A Multimodal Deception Detection Dataset and GSR-Guided Progressive Distillation for Non-Contact Deception Detection
abstract: Non-contact automatic deception detection remains challenging because visual and auditory deception cues often lack stable cross-subject patterns. In contrast, galvanic skin response (GSR) provides more reliable physiological cues and has been widely used in contact-based deception detection. In this work, we leverage stable deception-related knowledge in GSR to guide representation learning in non-contact modalities through cross-modal knowledge distillation. A key obstacle, however, is the lack of a suitable dataset for this setting. To address this, we introduce MuDD, a large-scale Multimodal Deception Detection dataset containing recordings from 130 participants over 690 minutes. In addition to video, audio, and GSR, MuDD also provides Photoplethysmography, heart rate, and personality traits, supporting broader scientific studies of deception. Based on this dataset, we propose GSR-guided Progressive Distillation (GPD), a cross-modal distillation framework for mitigating the negative transfer caused by the large modality mismatch between GSR and non-contact signals. The core innovation of GPD is the integration of progressive feature-level and digit-level distillation with dynamic routing, which allows the model to adaptively determine how teacher knowledge should be transferred during training, leading to more stable cross-modal knowledge transfer. Extensive experiments and visualizations show that GPD outperforms existing methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance on both deception detection and concealed-digit identification.

title: ForgeBorn License v1.0.1
abstract: The ForgeBorn License is a transparent, public-interest license framework designed to govern open AI infrastructure, protocols, and decentralized systems. It defines the terms under which systems, specifications, and implementations within the ForgeBorn ecosystem may be used, modified, and redistributed. This release represents version 1.0 of the license as published in the official Witchborn Systems repository. The DOI-backed record provides a stable, citable reference for the license text and its associated version.

title: Hidden-Test Distribution Science (HTDS): Core Field Specification, Staged Development Ladder, and Minimal Executable Kernel
abstract: Summary: HTDS Core Set v1.0 formalizes Hidden-Test Distribution Science as a lawful field for decision-making under hidden-test uncertainty. Rather than treating the hidden test as a secret answer key to be guessed, HTDS models a feasible family of hidden worlds constrained by public shadows, compresses those worlds by score-relevant equivalence, updates beliefs over them lawfully, and selects robust controllers under uncertainty. The archive introduces the core ontology of the field, including hidden-world families, public shadows, regime catalogs, controllers, equivalence classes, posterior world families, diversity measured through failure covariance, replayable receipts, and unresolved uncertainty scars. It includes the canonical core specifications, the staged development ladder from early hardened formulations through protocol, factorization, freeze, and runtime layers, and a minimal executable kernel that demonstrates the science in runnable form. HTDS is presented not as a leakage doctrine or leaderboard superstition, but as a scientific framework for lawful hidden-world inference, robust controller selection, and memory-bound freeze under partial observability. Keywords: Hidden-Test Distribution Science, HTDS, hidden-world inference, public shadows, score-relevant equivalence, controller robustness, partial observability, posterior world families, regime catalogs, failure covariance, lawful leaderboard inference, replayable freeze, uncertainty scars, executable scientific governance

title: Apparent Local Robustness Under Context-Reduced Interfaces: A Minimal Synthetic Stress Test
abstract: This technical note presents a minimal synthetic stress test on local robustness under reduced context interfaces in large language model inference. A controlled dataset of 100 multiple-choice instances is introduced across four evidence regimes: easy local retrieval, distributed evidence integration, conflict-sensitive update resolution, and position-sensitive retrieval. The same model is evaluated under three interfaces: FULL, RECENT, and a deterministic COMPRESSED interface retaining only the first sentence of each block. The main result is a clear regime-dependent dissociation: perfect local robustness is preserved in the easy regime, while strong interface-specific failures emerge outside it. The note is strictly diagnostic and local in scope, and argues that local benchmark robustness under a reduced context interface does not imply global behavioral equivalence across evidence regimes.
